title: Google's Android Earthquake Alerts detects the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake 5.31 s after origin and alerts over 16 million users on 23 April 2025; evaluation is Google-authored
summary: AEA detected the 23 April 2025 Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi quake in 5.31 s and alerted 16 million+ users (median 56 s warning for weak shaking); Google-authored evaluation; inland Take Action shortfall.
account: On 23 April 2025 the Mw 6.2 Marmara Ereğlisi earthquake struck offshore in the Sea of Marmara, Türkiye. Initial reports cited by the evaluation put shaking in Istanbul at MMI V. At least 359 people were injured, mostly from panic. Google's Android Earthquake Alerts (AEA) system uses the accelerometers of online Android phones. An on-phone detection algorithm flags sudden changes in acceleration. The system detected the event 5.31 seconds after its origin. It issued a first “Be Aware” alert 0.43 seconds later on an initial magnitude estimate of Mw 4.83. “Take Action” alerts followed as the estimate rose. Alerts reached more than 16 million Android users in Türkiye, Greece, Romania and Bulgaria. Warning times for weak shaking (MMI III) reached up to 150 seconds with a median of 56 seconds. The authors report 90% true positives and 99% precision. The final magnitude estimate saturated at Mw 6.04, so the “Take Action” polygon was too small. Inland populations that felt MMI V shaking received only the “Be Aware” warning before stronger shaking arrived. The evaluation (Nature Communications, 11 August 2026) and the system description (Science, 17 July 2025) are written by Google employees. So is the user-feedback data. The same system underestimated the 6 February 2023 Türkiye earthquakes. The BBC reported on 27 July 2025 that only 469 “Take Action” alerts were sent for the M7.8 event. 10 million people could have received one.
purpose: Crowd-sourced earthquake detection and early warning delivered to Android phones in countries without dense seismic networks. The alerts were the intended use.
deployer: Google (alerts delivered directly to Android users; launched in Türkiye in June 2021)
location: Sea of Marmara / Istanbul region, Türkiye (alerts also in Greece, Romania and Bulgaria)
taxonomy_note: An earthquake warning is read as a detection mechanism; no averted injury is documented.

ratings.reason: Google's feedback data say recipients were likely to drop, cover and hold on or warn others. No individual injury avoided is documented. The data are vendor-collected.
No organization's decision or operation is documented as changed by the alerts.

More than 16 million users were alerted with a median 56 s warning for weak shaking. “Take Action” alerts did not cover inland MMI V areas in time. No reduction in injuries is demonstrated. Evidence is vendor-authored.

ai_role.statement: The system itself generated the detection and the alerts. A few hundred phones triggered on the P wave. The system detected the event 5.31 s after origin and issued alerts within 0.43 s. Magnitude estimates were updated over the next 12 s. All performance figures and user-response data come from Google-authored papers (Mousavi et al. 2026; Allen et al. 2025). That is said plainly here. The only independent cited source, the BBC, concerns the 2023 underestimation. The read papers describe the detection as an on-phone algorithm that analyzes acceleration time series for sudden changes. They do not use the terms machine learning or artificial intelligence. Whether the system uses AI is not established by the sources.

Two-tier alerting (Be Aware, Take Action) delivered through the operating system
A population with high earthquake awareness after the 2023 Kahramanmaraş disaster, per the authors
must_hold: Enough stationary, charging phones near the epicentre to trigger early
Magnitude estimates that do not saturate below the true magnitude. This failed here at Mw 6.04 and failed badly in 2023.
Alerts that outrun S-wave arrival at the populated distance
Users who recognize and act on the alert

echoes.setting: Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.5 earthquakes, south-east Türkiye: magnitude estimated at 4.5–4.9; 469 Take Action alerts sent for the first quake when 10 million people could have received one (BBC)
Global operation over three years: alerts in 98 countries, about 60 events and 18 million alerts per month; 85% of alert recipients felt shaking (Science 2025, Google-authored)

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.
